summary:
NYXOS is a browser-based lunar south-pole landing-site navigator. It has a 3D simulator, a landing analysis page, a compare page and a mission-history page, and everything runs client-side with no server.

For a chosen lander, site and landing time, NYXOS computes Sun and Earth positions from JPL DE440, then traces horizons over NASA LOLA terrain, including the Moon’s curvature. It reports sunlight and Earth-visibility timelines, the longest dark and no-Earth spells, and the windows when a stay can start. It judges Safety (can we land), Operations (can we complete the mission) and Science (is it worth visiting) separately, against lander-specific limits such as Artemis HLS requirements. Users can compare up to six sites or six landing dates, and download reports.

NYXOS differs from other tools in three ways. It gives no combined score or ranking, so trade-offs stay visible. Every figure shows its source and data resolution, and unassessed hazards such as boulders are marked “Not evaluated” instead of guessed. A sensitivity test labels each verdict stable, sensitive or fragile. The ephemeris matches JPL Horizons within 0.001°, and modelled sunlight matches NASA illumination maps to about 3 percentage points RMS.

That makes polar landing decisions transparent, checkable and easy to explore.
details:
What it does and how it works: NYXOS is a web-based navigator for lunar south-pole landing sites. For a chosen site, lander and landing time, it answers three questions separately: can we land here (Safety), can we complete the mission (Operations), and is it worth visiting (Science). It takes Sun and Earth positions from JPL DE440 and traces the horizon over NASA LOLA terrain (about 20 m near a site), including the Moon’s curvature. From this it produces sunlight and Earth-visibility timelines, the longest dark and no-Earth spells, and the windows when a stay can start. Each constraint is rated Pass, Warning, Fail or Not evaluated against lander-specific limits (default: NASA Artemis HLS requirements), and a sensitivity test labels each verdict stable, sensitive or fragile. Users can explore a 3D simulator with a lander’s-eye view, compare up to six sites or six landing dates, export reports (HTML, PDF, CSV, JSON), and take a plain-language tour of Moon missions.

Benefits and intended impact: At the poles, a small shift in place or schedule can change the outcome. NYXOS makes that visible, so planners can see what a schedule slip costs or how quickly results change nearby. Every figure shows its source and data resolution, and the app states what it does not assess (boulders, small craters), so it supports early site assessment without claiming a site is certified safe.

Validation: The ephemeris matches JPL Horizons to within 0.001° across 847 samples. Modelled sunlight matches NASA’s average-illumination maps to about 3 percentage points RMS (correlation 0.977).

Tools: Vite, React, TypeScript, React Three Fiber and zustand, with all analysis running in the browser (no server). Python scripts build the data tiles from NASA LOLA, PGDA, LRO Diviner, Lunar Prospector, JPL and NASA SVS data. Hosted on Vercel.

Creativity: NYXOS deliberately gives no combined score or ranking, so trade-offs stay visible. The stable/sensitive/fragile label shows how far to trust each answer, and compare mode turns a lookup into a planning tool.

Factors considered: Data honesty (a Pass is capped at Warning where terrain data is too coarse), realistic lander limits, validation against NASA and JPL references, and scientific caution (cold or shadowed ground is not proof of ice).
